recipes.title: Berry good mornings
recipes.intro: Golden waffles, cool yoghurt and a generous handful of berries. A slow-morning favourite, even on a busy day.
steps: Prepare the toasting waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Divide the waffles between two plates. Spoon the yoghurt over them.
Add the strawberries, blueberries and sliced banana. Finish with a little honey and granola, if you like, and serve straight away.
recipes.twist: Swap the berries for whatever fruit is in season.

recipes.title: The Full English waffle
recipes.intro: Everything you love about a weekend fry-up, served on a crisp, golden waffle instead of toast.
ing: HP-style brown sauce or ketchup, to serve
steps: Grill the sausages and bacon until cooked through and golden, turning occasionally. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the mushrooms and tomatoes for 4 to 5 minutes until soft. Season with salt and pepper.
Fry the eggs in the same pan to your liking.
Prepare the toasting waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Place a waffle on each plate. Top with the mushrooms, tomatoes, bacon and sliced sausages, then crown with a fried egg.
Scatter over the chives and serve with your favourite sauce.
recipes.twist: Add a spoonful of baked beans on the side, or swap the bacon for black pudding.

recipes.title: Smoked salmon & soft cheese
recipes.intro: A smart, savoury brunch that's ready in minutes. Perfect for birthdays, Sunday mornings and Mother's Day trays.
ing: Small bunch of dill or chives
steps: Prepare the toasting waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Mix the soft cheese with a squeeze of lemon juice, a little chopped dill and plenty of black pepper.
Spread the cheese over the warm waffles.
Drape over the smoked salmon and top with capers, the rest of the herbs and a handful of watercress. Serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.twist: Top with a softly poached egg for a waffle take on eggs royale.

recipes.title: Ploughman's waffle
recipes.intro: The pub-lunch classic on a crisp, golden waffle: tangy cheddar, sweet pickle and a crunch of apple.
ing: Handful of watercress or mixed leaves
steps: Prepare the toasting waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Spread each warm waffle with pickle or chutney.
Layer over the ham, cheddar and apple slices.
Finish with the watercress and pickled onions. Serve straight away with a pot of tea.
recipes.twist: Swap the cheddar for Stilton and the apple for sliced pear.

recipes.title: Strawberries & cream hearts
recipes.intro: A taste of the British summer. Delicate heart waffles, sweet strawberries and a dollop of clotted cream.
ing: 1 pack Waffle Amour Dusted Heart Waffles
A few mint leaves, to decorate
steps: Toss the strawberries with the caster sugar and leave for 5 minutes until glossy and juicy.
Arrange the heart waffles on a serving plate or cake stand.
Spread each with a little jam, add a spoonful of clotted cream and top with the strawberries.
Decorate with mint leaves and serve with afternoon tea.
recipes.twist: Jam first or cream first? Try both and settle the debate once and for all.

recipes.title: Eton mess waffles
recipes.intro: The much-loved summer pudding, now with crisp heart waffles in the mix. Gloriously messy, as it should be.
ing: 1 pack Waffle Amour Dusted Heart Waffles
steps: Mash half the raspberries with the icing sugar to make a quick sauce.
Whip the cream with the vanilla until it holds soft peaks.
Roughly crush the meringue nests and fold them into the cream with the strawberries.
Place the heart waffles on plates, spoon over the cream mixture and finish with the remaining raspberries and a drizzle of raspberry sauce.
recipes.twist: In winter, swap the berries for poached rhubarb and a little stem ginger.

recipes.title: Banoffee waffles
recipes.intro: Banana, toffee and cream: the great British pudding, piled onto caramelised Liège sugar waffles.
ing: 3 tbsp caramel or dulce de leche
steps: Enjoy the waffles as they are, or warm them according to the instructions on your pack.
Spread the caramel over the waffles.
Top with the sliced banana and a spoonful of whipped cream.
Finish with grated dark chocolate and a pinch of cinnamon.
recipes.twist: Add a crumbled digestive biscuit for that classic banoffee-pie crunch.

recipes.title: Sticky toffee waffles
recipes.intro: All the comfort of sticky toffee pudding, ready in a fraction of the time. Made for chilly evenings.
ing: 2 scoops vanilla ice cream, or warm custard
steps: Put the butter, sugar and cream in a small pan over a low heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until thick and glossy. Add a pinch of salt.
Enjoy the waffles as they are, or warm them according to the instructions on your pack.
Place the waffles in bowls and scatter over the chopped dates.
Pour over the warm toffee sauce and serve with ice cream or custard.
recipes.twist: Stir a splash of brandy or rum into the sauce for a grown-up version.

recipes.title: Pancake Day lemon & sugar
recipes.intro: Shrove Tuesday's simplest classic, made with waffles. Sharp lemon, crunchy sugar, no flipping required.
steps: Prepare the toasting waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Spread each warm waffle with a little butter, if you like.
Squeeze over plenty of lemon juice and sprinkle with caster sugar.
Finish with a little grated lemon zest and eat straight away.
recipes.twist: Swap the lemon for orange, or drizzle with golden syrup instead.

recipes.title: Bonfire Night toffee apple
recipes.intro: Warm, cinnamon-spiced apples on a caramelised sugar waffle. Just the thing after the fireworks.
ing: 2 eating apples, such as Braeburn or Cox, cored and sliced
Warm custard or vanilla ice cream, to serve
steps: Melt the butter in a frying pan. Add the apples and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until starting to soften.
Sprinkle over the sugar and cinnamon and cook for a further 2 to 3 minutes until the apples are sticky and golden.
Enjoy the waffles as they are, or warm them according to the instructions on your pack.
Spoon the toffee apples over the waffles, add the custard or ice cream and scatter with hazelnuts.
recipes.twist: Add a handful of blackberries to the pan for an autumnal apple and blackberry twist.

recipes.title: Mince pie waffles
recipes.intro: A festive shortcut with all the flavours of a mince pie. Lovely on Christmas morning or as a quick pudding.
ing: 4 tbsp brandy butter, or crème fraîche
steps: Warm the mincemeat in a small pan for 2 to 3 minutes.
Enjoy the waffles as they are, or warm them according to the instructions on your pack.
Spoon the warm mincemeat over the waffles and top with a spoonful of brandy butter.
Finish with orange zest and a snowy dusting of icing sugar.
recipes.twist: Leftover Christmas pudding? Crumble it over the top instead of the mincemeat.

recipes.title: Black Forest waffles
recipes.intro: Chocolate, cherries and cream: a retro favourite that never goes out of style.
ing: 4 Waffle Amour Chocolate & Hazelnut Flavour Waffles
150 g cherries in syrup or kirsch, drained, with 2 tbsp syrup kept
steps: Prepare the waffles according to the instructions on your pack.
Warm the cherries with the reserved syrup in a small pan for 2 minutes.
Place two waffles on each plate and spoon over the cherries.
Top with whipped cream, a scattering of shaved chocolate and a fresh cherry.
recipes.twist: Stack the waffles with the cream and cherries between the layers for a mini gateau.

recipes.title: Choco waffle affogato
recipes.intro: A café-style treat at home. A chocolate waffle, a scoop of ice cream and a hot shot of espresso.
ing: 1 shot hot espresso, or 50 ml strong coffee
A few toasted flaked almonds, optional
steps: Place the waffle in a shallow bowl and top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Pour the hot espresso over the ice cream at the table.
Scatter over the almonds and enjoy while the ice cream melts into the waffle.
recipes.twist: For a child-friendly version, swap the espresso for warm chocolate sauce.
